issues.description: Resolver no longer marks requirements as prepared, leaving an unstated invariant break for downstream consumers.
issues.detail: The removed block set `req.prepared = True` and `req.needs_more_preparation = False` after resolve. The new code returns req_set without touching either flag, relying on callers to invoke `prepare_linked_requirements_more`. The invariant 'after resolver.resolve, requirements are prepared' is now silently violated. State the new contract in a docstring on resolve(), or have prepare_linked_requirements_more set those flags itself.

issues.description: Three call sites duplicate the same `prepare_linked_requirements_more` call with no shared abstraction.
issues.detail: install.py, download.py, and wheel.py each independently call `preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(requirement_set.requirements.values())` at a specific point in their flow. A future command (e.g. `pip lock`) that forgets this call will silently regress to the old behavior. Either fold it into a RequirementSet method or document the obligation prominently on the resolver's return value.

issues.description: `set_dist` bypasses the existing precedence rules in `get_dist` without documenting why it wins.
issues.detail: `get_dist` previously dispatched on `metadata_directory`, `local_file_path`, etc. The new `self._distribution` short-circuits all of them with no comment explaining the ordering. If a later code path populates `metadata_directory` after `set_dist` was called with stale metadata, the stale value silently wins. State the invariant: '_distribution, once set, is the authoritative dist for this requirement's lifetime.'

issues.description: `download_info` is unconditionally set from `req.link` and `req.source_dir` with no audit of what `source_dir` is during metadata-only fetch.
issues.detail: In dry-run / metadata-only mode, `req.source_dir` may be unset or point to a transient location, yet `direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir)` is called unconditionally. The PR description claims this enables `pip lock` and `--report`, but there is no test or assertion showing the resulting `DirectUrl` is correct for a never-downloaded wheel. Verify and document the precondition.

issues.description: No literate comment explaining why the old in-resolver preparation was removed.
issues.detail: The deletion in resolver.py is the architectural heart of the change: 'preparation moves out of resolve and into each command.' A careful reader of resolver.py alone cannot recover that rationale. A short block comment at the deletion site, or in the resolve() docstring, would prevent a future contributor from 'helpfully' restoring the loop and re-introducing the bug #12603 exists to fix.

issues.description: `set_dist` has no docstring and no validation that the distribution matches the requirement.
issues.detail: A one-line setter that mutates authoritative state deserves at minimum a docstring stating the contract: when it is legal to call, whether re-setting is allowed, and the relationship to `metadata_directory`. As written, a caller can `set_dist(unrelated_dist)` and `get_dist` will return it. Cheap to fix; expensive to debug later.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The change correctly moves "more preparation" out of the resolver and into each command, which is the right architectural move to fix #12603. But the new contract is nowhere stated: the resolver no longer sets `req.prepared` / `needs_more_preparation`, three commands duplicate the same call with no shared abstraction, and `set_dist` / the new `download_info` assignment introduce authoritative state mutations without docstrings or invariant comments. The algorithm is fine; the literate-programming layer is missing. Add docstrings on `resolve()`, `set_dist`, and the prepare.py block, and verify `source_dir` is meaningful at the dry-run call site.
